novelty.justification: The claim’s novelty route is a mechanism-level relationship: “different components track different distance dimensions,” specifically predicting semantic/concept-feature transfer from lexical or genetic distance and syntactic-circuit transfer from word-order or morphological distance. Searches for “typological distance cross-lingual circuit transfer,” “multilingual steering vector transfer language similarity,” and “SAE features cross-lingual typology” found closest precedents in Lauscher et al.’s From Zero to Hero (2020), which relates linguistic similarity to task-level transfer, and CLaS-Bench (2026), which evaluates multilingual steering and finds language-family clustering, but neither attributes retained causal effects of multiple interpretable component types to distinct typological sub-distances. Moving from those works to component-wise causal transfer is a natural but non-trivial extension that changes the unit of analysis and integrates established typology, steering, SAE, and circuit ideas rather than introducing an entirely new mechanistic paradigm, supporting standard novelty.
